signals.text: The user wants a command-line tool that counts the words in a text file.
signals.possible_indication: Core new capability; the existing 'hello' package has no user-facing command yet.

signals.text: The user passes the path to a text file to the tool.
signals.possible_indication: Input is a single file path given at invocation; behavior for missing, unreadable or non-text files is not stated.

signals.text: The tool prints the number of words the file contains.
signals.possible_indication: Output is a single count; what counts as a 'word' is not defined and is assumed to follow the common whitespace-separated convention.

signals.text: The project should use the latest version of Python.
signals.possible_indication: The existing .python-version and pyproject.toml may need to target the newest stable Python release.

signals.text: The project should follow best practices for project structure and code quality.
signals.possible_indication: Implies an enforceable quality bar; AGENTS.md currently has an empty Toolchain table and a Quality Gate that must not be bypassed.

signals.text: The project should include a README.md explaining how to install and run the CLI.
signals.possible_indication: README.md already exists; the change is adding install and run instructions for the new CLI, not creating the file.

DISCOVER.core_issue: Users have no way to get the word count of a text file from the 'hello' project; they want to run a command with a file path and see how many words it contains.
DISCOVER.impact_value: Delivers the project's first user-facing capability, on a current Python version and with a clear, documented install-and-run path so new users can adopt it without help.
DISCOVER.discovery_method: Written intent from the project owner, read against the existing tracked files and AGENTS.md.
DISCOVER.pattern_dependencies: Counting words from a file is the central opportunity. The usage documentation depends on it, since the README can only explain how to install and run a command that exists. The quality standards apply across both: they set the Python version and the quality bar the tool and its documentation must meet.
